record.paper_title: On some open problems of number theory
record.original_question: Are there infinitely many prime numbers of the form x^2 + 1, with x an integer?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Determine whether there exist infinitely many positive integers $x$ such that $x^2 + 1$ is a prime number. Equivalently, is the set $\{p \text{ prime} : p = x^2 + 1 \text{ for some } x \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ infinite?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a classical and famous open problem in number theory, known as Landau's problem (one of the four problems Landau posed in 1912). It remains unsolved as of 2026; it is not known whether there are infinitely many primes of the form $n^2+1$. Iwaniec (1978) showed infinitely many $n$ for which $n^2+1$ has at most two prime factors.

status_evidence.title: Landau's problems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Are there infinitely many primes of the form n^2 + 1? All four problems remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of infinitely many primes of the form n^2+1 is one of Landau's problems and remains open.
